chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the bequest, and he said: “It is a duty upon every Muslim.”

key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: bequest or will made regarding one’s affairs and estate
key_terms.حَقٌّ: a binding due or established obligation
key_terms.كُلِّ مُسْلِمٍ: every Muslim without exception in the general sense of the ruling

ai.seo_question: Is making a will obligatory for every Muslim in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that making a bequest is a binding responsibility upon every Muslim. It highlights the legal and moral importance of arranging one's affairs through a will, especially in matters connected to rights and property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5411 - Muhammad ibn Al-Fudayl narrated from Abu Al-Sabbah Al-Kinani from Abu Abdullah Imam Al-Sadiq (as), who said: I asked Imam (as) about making a will.
Imam (as) said: "It is a duty upon every Muslim."
